issues.description: WriterLock.acquire() performs a genuine TOCTOU (time-of-check-to-time-of-use) race: exists()/is_live() check, then a decision, then an unconditional plain-text write (no O_CREAT|O_EXCL, no atomic rename) -- allowing multiple concurrent agents to all believe they hold exclusive write ownership simultaneously. A second, related bug: a stale (expired-lease) owner's own in-memory WriterLock object can later call .heartbeat() or .release() and unconditionally overwrite a DIFFERENT agent's legitimately-reclaimed lock, because neither method re-validates lock_id/ownership against what is actually currently on disk before writing -- .release()'s owned_by() check only compares against the stale caller's own remembered owner field, never re-reading the live file.

Second race reproduced via a sequential stale_owner_probe.py: agent-1 acquires with lease_minutes=0 (instant expiry) -> agent-2 correctly reclaims -> agent-1's original stale WriterLock object calls .heartbeat() -> on-disk owner silently reverts from agent-2 to agent-1, and agent-1.release(owner='agent-1') then marks agent-2's still-active lock 'released'.

issues.subsystem: ultimate_pipeline/contracts/writer_lock.py -- fresh-lock partial-publication reader race (distinct from GAP-024)
issues.description: WriterLock.acquire()'s O_EXCL create (line 129: os.open(lock_path, O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY|O_BINARY)) makes the lock pathname visible at size 0 BEFORE the subsequent fdopen/write/flush/fsync (lines 149-152) complete writing the payload. A losing process gets FileExistsError (line 130), immediately calls cls.load() (line 132), and load()'s json.loads(path.read_text()) (line 203) raises JSONDecodeError on the empty/torn file. Only FileNotFoundError was caught (lines 133-136); JSONDecodeError (a ValueError) propagated out of acquire() -> the multiprocessing worker (_writer_lock_mp_worker.py:41-42) reported 'error' -> tests/unit/test_writer_lock_concurrency.py:78 'assert not errors' failed on Linux CI with JSONDecodeError('Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)'). IMPORTANT: this is a NEW residual gap INTRODUCED by the GAP-024 O_EXCL fix (the visible-before-written window for readers that the old exists()-check-then-write sequence did not create, because the old code wrote content at a path that was only raced after being fully written, or claimed exclusivity by winning the check). It must NOT be conflated with GAP-024: GAP-024 remains fixed (O_EXCL is still the sole exclusivity authority; exactly-one-winner still holds); GAP-029 is the reader-side torn-read window that same fix opened. Fix: in acquire()'s FileExistsError branch, classify load() outcomes three ways -- FileNotFoundError keeps the existing continue/retry; (ValueError, TypeError) (empty file, torn JSON, JSON list, extra-key TypeError from from_dict) enters a bounded fresh-publication re-read sub-loop (100 x 0.005s = ~500ms ceiling, _FRESH_PUBLISH_MAX_REREADS/_FRESH_PUBLISH_REREAD_DELAY_S documented next to _ACQUIRE_MAX_ATTEMPTS) that recovers if the winner finishes publishing, continues the outer O_EXCL loop if the file vanishes, and otherwise raises a DISTINCT RuntimeError 'writer.lock at {path} exists but is not readable JSON; refusing to acquire or delete it' (RuntimeError -> mp worker 'blocked', deliberately NOT containing 'Writer lock held by', and the file is NEVER unlinked in this state); a successful load falls through to the unchanged live->held / not-live->unlink+retry path. load(), from_dict(), save(), release(), heartbeat(), _assert_still_current(), is_live/is_malformed/_parse_iso, the acquire() signature, SCHEMA_VERSION, O_EXCL flags, and _ACQUIRE_MAX_ATTEMPTS are all untouched.
issues.proof: Mechanically reproduced by the new GAP-029 widened-timing test with the production fix temporarily stashed (git stash push -- ultimate_pipeline/contracts/writer_lock.py): test_widened_fresh_publication_contender_never_sees_partial_json FAILED on iteration 0 with all 8 contender processes reporting error=JSONDecodeError('Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)') -- the exact signature observed on Linux CI. With the fix restored, the same test passes (4/4 in the new module). The widened window is deterministic: a top-level delayed_publish_worker claims the path via raw O_CREAT|O_EXCL (pathname visible, size 0), holds it empty 0.25s (above the real ~microsecond window, far below the 500ms re-read budget), then writes a pre-built valid live lock JSON; 8 real acquire_worker processes are released into that window.
issues.scientific_runtime_consequence: Without the fix, a legitimate lock contender can crash out of acquire() with an uncaught JSONDecodeError whenever it reads the winner's lock file during the microsecond-to-millisecond fresh-publication window -- surfacing as an indeterminate worker 'error' rather than a clean 'blocked'. This does NOT break single-writer exclusivity (the loser never wins; it errors), but it converts a deterministic contention outcome into flaky CI and could mislead an operator into thinking the lock system is broken when exclusivity is actually intact. The fail-closed branch added here also protects against a genuinely malformed persistent lock being silently deleted by a would-be reclaimer.

issues.subsystem: tools/tile_frame_consistency.py (O3) + full-grid tile cook evidence -- latent ~170-270m north-south tile-seam misplacement
issues.description: Independently discovered and numerically demonstrated by docs/verify-o3-tile-frame-fullgrid-cook-20260929 (2026-09-29), not by O3 itself. O3's own seam check (tools/tile_frame_consistency.py) is weaker than a real geometric seam check: it compares each tile's raw, independently-OSM2World-auto-centered local bounding box against its neighbor's, never applying any tile-placement transform, and its per-pair 'status' field is dead code (always 'INCOMPLETE', never gates the top-level PASS/FAIL). The verifying subagent instead built a ground-truth-anchored check: for 4 adjacent tile pairs from the current-pin full-grid cook (reports/production_readiness/20260924T100614Z_FULL_GRID_TILE_FBX_COOK/), it computed each named OSM building's true lat/lon centroid, projected it into the pipeline's native frame, subtracted the registry rebase offset, matched it to its OSM2World-exported mesh object by name (discovering and correcting for OSM2World's OBJ south-positive Z axis via two independent building-pair distance cross-checks, 1.4% agreement), and computed the per-tile median residual offset needed on top of the only tile-placement convention this codebase documents (tx*1000, ty*1000).
issues.proof: Both north-south adjacent pairs showed a statistically overwhelming, non-noise offset inconsistency: tile_8_8 vs tile_8_9 (y/north-south) delta=176.5m, standard error ~13.9m (~12.7 sigma); tile_7_8 vs tile_7_9 (y/north-south) delta=270.1m, standard error ~21.5m (~12.6 sigma). The east-west pair (tile_7_8 vs tile_8_8, x-axis) was comparatively closer to consistent (46.1m vs ~16.5m noise budget -- borderline). Root cause: OSM2World auto-centers every tile's output independently around its own local (0,0), regardless of the tile's true geographic position, and blender_convert.py applies zero translation on OBJ to FBX -- so nothing anywhere in the actual artifact chain places these 20 tiles in a shared frame. Each tile's own internal geometry is plausible and the per-tile roundtrip evidence (20/20 PASS) is real; the defect only appears when tiles are assembled using the pipeline's documented placement convention.
issues.scientific_runtime_consequence: If the 20 currently-cooked tiles were assembled into a shared UE4/CARLA scene using the only placement convention this codebase documents, north-south-adjacent tiles would be visibly misaligned by roughly 170-270m -- most of a full tile width. This is a real, previously-undetected, numerically-demonstrated defect in the tile-based visual (buildings-only, non-road-truth) cooking path, not a false positive; O3's own check could never have caught it since it never introduces an independent ground-truth reference.

issues.subsystem: ultimate_pipeline/contracts/writer_lock.py -- load() leaked raw JSONDecodeError/TypeError instead of failing closed with RuntimeError
issues.description: Two related bugs found during this integration (distinct from, and not covered by, GAP-024/GAP-029): (1) WriterLock.load() called json.loads(path.read_text()) and cls.from_dict(data) with no exception handling at all -- a corrupt, zero-byte, or non-object-JSON (e.g. a JSON list) lock file raised a raw json.JSONDecodeError/UnicodeDecodeError/TypeError directly out of load(), inconsistent with this module's established fail-closed philosophy (compare acquire()'s own distinct 'not readable JSON; refusing to acquire or delete it' RuntimeError).
